text:
The plate is about 26 cm across and spans roughly 350 px, so 1 cm is about 13.5 px. The two corn pieces are each about 95 px across, or about 7 cm. Each is a cross-cut corn cob segment about 3 cm thick.

Volume of each piece: radius 3.5 cm, so the area is about 38 cm² and the volume about 115 cm³ for a 3 cm height. The cob core takes up some of that, and the kernels plus cob are fairly dense at about 0.8 g/cm³. That gives roughly 90 g per piece, so about 180 g for both, though the pieces may be shorter than 3 cm. At 2.5 cm thick each would weigh about 75 g, so I'll use about 150 g in total.

Boiled corn on the cob, cob included, is about 90–100 kcal per 100 g. The cob is not edible, but the kcal value per 100 g of the whole piece is lower, around 85.
